items.title: [draft] Programmatic KV-cache control from Dynamo

labels.name: router
labels.description: Relates to routing, KV-aware routing, etc.

items.body:
## Summary

Give Dynamo a programmatic control path for KV-cache behavior on inference engines.

Router-to-engine hints are the first step, not the final feature. The hint path carries typed cache intent with a routed request. The engine validates that intent and applies it through its native cache machinery.

This path unlocks programmatic cache actions such as prefetch, demote, and dereference. Dynamo can then coordinate cache behavior from session lifecycle, cache pressure, reuse, and cluster state.

## Why this matters

Dynamo has the global view. It knows request placement, session history, worker load, cache locality, and available remote copies.

The inference engine has the local view. It owns radix state, reference counts, cache tiers, transfer connectors, and request safety.

Today most cache changes happen as side effects of request execution and eviction. Dynamo can choose a worker, but it cannot express the desired cache action cleanly. Backend-specific fields and separate control APIs make this problem harder for every new action.

The hint path creates one boundary between policy and mechanism:

- Dynamo decides what cache behavior is useful and when to request it.
- The engine decides how to apply that behavior safely on its cache implementation.

## Control flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Session lifecycle and cache state"] --> B["Dynamo routing policy"]
    B --> C["Normal worker selection"]
    C --> D["Attach optional KV action hints"]
    D --> E["Backend request adapter"]
    E --> F["Engine hint surface"]
    F --> G["Cache manager and storage tiers"]
    G --> H["Cache events and action results"]
    H --> B
```

`KvHints` describe cache behavior on the selected engine. The selected engine receives only actions that it supports. The backend adapter maps the shared request into the native vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM interface. The engine hint surface then calls the correct cache or transfer component.

## Phase 1: Establish the hint path

The first milestone creates one shared path from Dynamo to an engine:

- one typed `KvHints` envelope on the routed request
- independent action fields that can be combined
- engine discovery of supported actions
- filtering after worker selection
- backend-specific lowering
- an engine-owned handler surface

This is infrastructure for cache control. It removes the need for a new envelope, side channel, or router result type for each action.

## Phase 2: Add programmatic cache actions

Each action uses the same path but keeps its own semantics and engine implementation.

Example actions - not an exhaustive list. Just some initial POCs
| Action | Programmatic intent |
| --- | --- |
| Prefetch | Bring reusable KV to the selected engine or a faster tier before it is needed. |
| Demote | Move selected KV from a hot tier to a lower tier to recover capacity without losing reuse. |
| Dereference | Release cache ownership or protection so normal eviction can reclaim the KV. |

Other actions can use the same path after their ownership and failure semantics are clear.

These actions are distinct. Dereference does not mean physical deletion. Demotion requires safe completion before hot-tier state is released. Prefetch must identify reusable KV without changing request correctness.

## Phase 3: Build router policies on these actions

The action surface makes cache policy programmable. Initial policy inputs can include:

- compaction and session completion
- cache pressure and tier capacity
- recent reuse and recompute cost
- session idle time and expected continuation
- target locality and remote KV availability

Example policies include proactive continuation prefetch, pressure-driven demotion, compaction cleanup, and cross-worker KV reuse. Each policy remains separate from the engine action that it invokes. 

A tangible example here is a session aware routing strategy like Thunderagent that is able to also influence KV cache via hints during its scheduling behavior

## Safety and failure behavior

- Hints never carry correctness-critical request data.
- An unsupported or unavailable action follows the normal engine path.
- The engine remains the source of truth for references, generations, residency, and transfer completion.
- Each action reports accepted, applied, ignored, failed, and fallback outcomes.
- Action failures do not suppress other independent hints.

## Non-goals

- Define all cache-action semantics in one issue or one pull request.
- Standardize cache-manager internals across engines.
- Let Dynamo mutate engine cache state directly.
- Add a separate REST or RPC control plane for every action.
- Require every backend to support every action.

## Acceptance criteria

- Dynamo has one router-to-engine path for programmatic KV-cache intent.
- A new cache action does not require another ad hoc envelope or selection type.
- Each engine can expose and implement its supported action subset.
- Router policies can request actions after normal worker selection.
- Action logic stays isolated in the backend adapter and engine hint surface.
- Metrics connect each requested action to its engine result and fallback path.
- The empty hint path adds no per-token work and no measurable request-path regression.
- Each action receives separate safety and performance validation before default enablement.

## Current work

- Shared Dynamo hint path: https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/pull/13134
- Request-derived action example in Dynamo: https://github.com/ishandhanani/dynamo/pull/7
- Engine-side hint surface in SGLang: https://github.com/ishandhanani/sglang/pull/8

These changes establish the control path. Programmatic prefetch, demotion, dereference, and future cache policies build on that foundation.

items.title: [BUG]: KV cache block events never published to ZMQ despite kv-events-config being set (vLLM v1 engine)

labels.name: router
labels.description: Relates to routing, KV-aware routing, etc.

items.body:
## Summary

When `--kv-events-config` is passed to `dynamo.vllm` with `publisher: zmq` and `enable_kv_cache_events: true`, the ZMQ publisher is configured and the startup log confirms the config is parsed correctly — but **zero KV block events are ever published**. As a result, the KV cache-aware router receives no block announcements and cannot steer requests based on prefix affinity.

## Environment

| Component | Version |
|---|---|
| Dynamo image | `dynamo-vllm-runtime:1.3.0-dev.1-cuda13` |
| vLLM engine | v0.22.0 (V1 engine) |
| Models tested | `google/gemma-3-27b-it-FP8`, `Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B-FP8` |
| Deployment | Kubernetes (DynamoGraphDeployment CRD) |
| Router mode | `--router-mode=kv` (frontend) |

## Configuration

Worker args passed to `dynamo.vllm`:
```
--kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","topic":"kv-events","endpoint":"tcp://*:20080","enable_kv_cache_events":true,"buffer_steps":10000,"hwm":100000,"max_queue_size":100000}'
```

Frontend: `--router-mode=kv`

## Actual behaviour

Startup log confirms the config is recognised:
```
INFO Using kv_events_config for publishing vLLM kv events over zmq:
  KVEventsConfig(enable_kv_cache_events=True, publisher='zmq',
  endpoint='tcp://*:20080', topic='kv-events', ...)
```

But:
- Metric `dynamo_component_kv_publisher_engines_published_events` stays at **0** across all workers
- No `kv_publisher` or ZMQ event log lines appear in worker stdout after startup
- Router routing decisions show **0 host_pinned blocks** and **0 disk blocks** for every worker
- Prefix cache hit rates (10–56%) are present, but these reflect per-worker local APC only, not cross-worker sharing

## Expected behaviour

Every KV block store/evict in the vLLM engine should trigger a callback that publishes a ZMQ block event. The router should receive these events and use them to route prefix-matching requests to whichever worker holds the matching blocks.

## Hypothesis — broken callback hookup with vLLM v1

The callback that Dynamo registers with the vLLM engine to receive KV block lifecycle notifications appears to be a no-op against the **vLLM v1 engine** (`AsyncLLM` / `EngineCore` IPC architecture, introduced ~v0.6).

In vLLM v0 (`LLMEngine`), the hookup targeted the old internal API (e.g. `engine.add_kv_event_handler`). The v1 engine changed the KV cache management and executor internals. If the callback registration still targets the v0 API surface, the callback silently never fires — no error, no events, no routing.

Supporting evidence: there are no log lines after startup indicating the callback was successfully wired into the engine's block table. The publisher object is constructed but never receives data.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Deploy `dynamo.vllm` with `--kv-events-config '{"publisher":"zmq","enable_kv_cache_events":true,...}'`
2. Configure frontend with `--router-mode=kv`
3. Send requests with repeated long system prompts
4. Check metric `dynamo_component_kv_publisher_engines_published_events` — stays at 0
5. Check router logs for `host_pinned` block counts — stays at 0

## Impact

KV cache-aware routing is completely non-functional with the vLLM v1 engine. All requests are routed without KV affinity. Long-context workloads (15k–60k token prompts) that would benefit most from cross-replica prefix reuse get none of it.

## Additional context

Local per-worker APC works because vLLM v0.22.0 enables prefix caching by default. The issue is specifically the **event publishing path** from the worker to the ZMQ router — the publisher is initialised but the vLLM v1 engine never calls the event callback that feeds it.

items.title: [BUG]: vllm disagg KV-cache OOM in AIC-generated DGD

labels.name: deployment::k8s
labels.description: Relates to dynamo deployment in kubernetes

items.body:
### Describe the Bug

Bug from [recipe testing](https://github.com/ashnamehrotra/dynamo/blob/12924f3d404022fafa1111f01f09f06523593cd6/deploy/_recipe-tests/TESTING.md):

> ### Summary
> When `DGDR` runs the AIC profiler for a vllm disaggregated topology, the generated `DynamoGraphDeployment` configures `max_model_len=131072` for prefill workers but does not allocate enough GPU memory for the corresponding KV cache. All prefill workers enter `CrashLoopBackOff` immediately on startup.
>
> ### Reproduction
> Recipe: `l3-70b-vllm-dis` (in `deploy/_recipe-tests/recipes.tsv`)
>
> ```yaml
> apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1beta1
> kind: DynamoGraphDeploymentRequest
> spec:
>   model: nvidia/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8
>   backend: vllm
>   image: nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/dynamo-planner:1.1.1
>   autoApply: true
>   hardware: { totalGpus: 8 }
>   modelCache: { pvcName: model-cache, pvcModelPath: hub/models--nvidia--Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8/snapshots/07a08be3..., pvcMountPath: /home/dynamo/.cache/huggingface }
> ```
>
> Or via the e2e suite:
> ```bash
> cd deploy/_recipe-tests && ./run-matrix.sh l3-70b-vllm-dis
> ```
>
> ### Observed
> - Profiling job completes successfully (40s).
> - DGDR transitions to `Deploying`, generates DGD `vllm-disagg-<hash>`.
> - All four `*-vllmprefillworker-*` pods enter `CrashLoopBackOff` and never become Ready.
> - DGDR remains `Deploying` until the test's 90-min timeout.
>
> ### Error
> ```
> ValueError: To serve at least one request with the model's max seq len (131072),
> 20.0 GiB KV cache is needed, which is larger than the available KV cache memory (1.15 GiB).
> Based on the available memory, the estimated maximum model length is 7536.
> Try increasing `gpu_memory_utilization` or decreasing `max_model_len` when initializing the engine.
> ```
> Source: `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py:644 _check_enough_kv_cache_memory`
>
> ### Expected
> AIC profiler should either:
> - Set `max_model_len` to a value that fits within the available KV cache budget, OR
> - Increase `gpu_memory_utilization` / set explicit `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, OR
> - Refuse to emit a config it knows will OOM
>
> ### Environment
> Image: `nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/dynamo-planner:1.1.1`. AKS cluster, H100 SXM5 80GB ×8.

### Steps to Reproduce

> ### Reproduction
> Recipe: `l3-70b-vllm-dis` (in `deploy/_recipe-tests/recipes.tsv`)
>
> ```yaml
> apiVersion: nvidia.com/v1beta1
> kind: DynamoGraphDeploymentRequest
> spec:
>   model: nvidia/Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8
>   backend: vllm
>   image: nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/dynamo-planner:1.1.1
>   autoApply: true
>   hardware: { totalGpus: 8 }
>   modelCache: { pvcName: model-cache, pvcModelPath: hub/models--nvidia--Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8/snapshots/07a08be3..., pvcMountPath: /home/dynamo/.cache/huggingface }
> ```
>
> Or via the e2e suite:
> ```bash
> cd deploy/_recipe-tests && ./run-matrix.sh l3-70b-vllm-dis
> ```
>

### Expected Behavior

  > ### Expected
> AIC profiler should either:
> - Set `max_model_len` to a value that fits within the available KV cache budget, OR
> - Increase `gpu_memory_utilization` / set explicit `kv_cache_memory_bytes`, OR
> - Refuse to emit a config it knows will OOM

### Actual Behavior

> ### Observed
> - Profiling job completes successfully (40s).
> - DGDR transitions to `Deploying`, generates DGD `vllm-disagg-<hash>`.
> - All four `*-vllmprefillworker-*` pods enter `CrashLoopBackOff` and never become Ready.
> - DGDR remains `Deploying` until the test's 90-min timeout.

### Environment

Image: `nvcr.io/nvidia/ai-dynamo/dynamo-planner:1.1.1`. AKS cluster, H100 SXM5 80GB ×8.

items.title: [FEATURE]: Layerwise KV Cache Transfer for Disaggregated TensorRT-LLM Serving
items.body:
### Feature request

Enabling layerwise KV cache transfer in TensorRT-LLM for disaggregated serving.

### Describe the problem you're encountering

The TTFT of TensorRT-LLM for long contexts is markedly slower than that of vLLM with layer-wise KV transfer.

### Describe alternatives you've tried

Have tried dynamo’s vLLM backend with LMCache support, but the overall performance of vllm is significantly inferior to tensorrt-llm, offering no practical benefit.

We've come across a similar issue from the past, and it looks like there's already a viable solution：https://github.com/ai-dynamo/dynamo/issues/2436
